steps.title: The same root, poured into a different pattern
body: You already know that a root can carry more than one word — ك-ت-ب gives you كَتَبَ, كِتَاب, and مَكْتَبَة. A verb's root works the same way, except here the different "pattern" changes the verb itself, not just the part of speech: the same three consonants can build ten distinct verb patterns, each with its own tendency of meaning.

Five of the ten patterns are already sitting in words you know how to write: جَرَّبَ (to try), سَافَرَ (to travel), تَكَلَّمَ (to speak), اِشْتَرَى (to buy), and اِسْتَيْقَظَ (to wake up). You've been using all five since A1/A2 — this lesson just names the pattern underneath each one.

Patterns aren't fixed rules — they're strong tendencies. Form II often makes a verb causative or intensive, Form III often adds a reciprocal or effort-toward-someone sense, Form V is often the reflexive of Form II, Form VIII often a middle-voice/reflexive sense, Form X often "to seek or consider X." A specific root can drift from the textbook tendency into its own lexicalized meaning — اِشْتَرَى just means "to buy," not something more literally reflexive.

steps.title: Five patterns you already know
steps.intro: Read each sentence, then check which verb form it uses. Tap 🔊 to hear any line.

steps.title: Spot the pattern
steps.prompt: جَرَّبَ (to try) has a doubled middle letter. Which form is that?
steps.explanation: فَعَّلَ doubles the middle root letter (the shaddah on the ر in جَرَّبَ) — the mark of Form II.

steps.title: Spot the pattern
steps.prompt: اِسْتَيْقَظَ (to wake up) starts with اِسْتَ. Which form is that?
steps.explanation: اِسْتَفْعَلَ prefixes اِسْتَ to the root — the same prefix you can see on اِسْتَيْقَظَ.

steps.title: Meaning tendencies
steps.prompt: تَكَلَّمَ is Form V — تَ added to Form II's own pattern. What does Form V often mean?

options.label: The reflexive of Form II — doing (or becoming) that action to/for yourself
Seeking or considering something to be true
A color or a physical defect

steps.explanation: Form V's تَ prefix is the same reflexive تَ you'll see again on Form VI — Form V takes Form II's causative/intensive sense and turns it back on the subject.

steps.title: You've had your first look at derived verb forms
steps.message: Five forms, all built from verbs you already knew how to write — the same shared-DNA idea as root & pattern, now applied to how a verb itself changes shape. The other four forms (IV, VI, VII, IX) are still ahead.
